summary.intent: Bring the README, CONTRIBUTING, ARCHITECTURE and related docs up to date with the code after PR #369, and remove a recurring merge-conflict source in docs/errors.md.
summary.outcome: Updated README quick start, CONTRIBUTING (setup, recipes, checklist), docs/architecture/release.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, and removed the hand-maintained count line from docs/errors.md. The doc build and the tests that read docs/errors.md were run, and the docs PR was shipped stacked on #369.

repo: docs/errors.md had a hand-maintained count line that conflicted on every PR adding an error code; nothing in the repo read or enforced it, so it was safe to delete.
Lint tests skip locally when the required tools are missing (they run in CI), and CONTRIBUTING now documents this.
The docs build is clean after the edits.
callisto-model is an MIT library crate that others can depend on, and it has about 955 undocumented public items.
Docs work is done on a branch rebased on the CI PR (#369), and the docs PR is stacked on it.

code.finding: Count line removed because no test or tooling enforces it; the tests that read this file still pass.

workflow: Verify doc claims against the actual code or behavior (for example the lint-test local skip, and README claims against docs) before writing them.
Fix recurring pain at the source, such as a hand-maintained count that conflicts on every PR, rather than just resolving it each time.
When a guard rejects a multi-change script in Bash, apply the changes one at a time with the editor tool.
Stacking the docs PR on the open CI PR keeps related changes reviewable separately.

friction: The command guard rejected the script text used to update CONTRIBUTING in bulk, so each change had to be applied as a separate edit.
open_items: About 955 public items in callisto-model lack docs; whether to take on that documentation effort was left as a decision for the user.
The docs PR is stacked on #369 and depends on it being merged first.
